exam.subject: Geography
exam.title: Warsay Yikealo Secondary School, Sawa Department of Geography 2nd Semester Final (Model) Examination 2015-2016

questions.stem: The **geographical location** of Saho ethnic group is mainly found in the zones of:

options.C: Northern Red Sea and Southern Red Sea

explanation_steps: The Saho ethnic group in Eritrea primarily inhabits the foothills of the **eastern escarpment** and the coastal plains. Geographically, this corresponds to the **Debub** (Southern) and **Northern Red Sea** zones.

questions.stem: The constant change of temperature associated with the **rotation** of the earth is:
explanation_steps: The **daily march of temperature** refers to the hourly changes in temperature over a 24-hour period, which is directly caused by the Earth's rotation on its axis, leading to the cycle of day and night.

questions.stem: Identify the **correct** statement.

options.A: the same latitudinal location of different altitudes has the same temperature.
options.B: temperature and pressure differences make winds to blow into different directions
options.C: seasonal temperature distribution is the function of altitude
options.D: temperature of Eritrea is more modified by latitudinal factor than altitude
options.E: ITCZ located south of Eritrea during summer season

explanation_steps: Wind is caused by the movement of air from areas of high pressure to areas of low pressure, which is driven by temperature differences. Therefore, temperature and pressure differences are the fundamental causes of wind direction.

questions.stem: Which of the following is **outside** the universe?
explanation_steps: The **Universe** is defined as the totality of all space, time, matter, and energy. By definition, anything that exists physically (like plants, stars, or planets) is part of the universe. Therefore, nothing is 'outside' it.

questions.stem: Before the coming of Italian colonial rule the people of Eritrea **derived materials** from:
explanation_steps: Before the Italian colonial era, Eritrea did not have modern industries. People relied on **cottage industries** (traditional crafts like weaving, pottery, and metalwork) to produce the materials and tools they needed for daily life.

questions.stem: One of the following is considered as **single feature regions**:
explanation_steps: **Single-feature regions** are areas defined based on one specific characteristic, such as climate, language, or economic activity. Both economic regions and climate regions are primary examples of formal regions defined by a single broad feature.

questions.stem: One of the following is **not** the consequence of global warming
explanation_steps: Global warming is an atmospheric phenomenon that leads to climate-related issues like droughts and melting polar ice. **Earthquakes** are tectonic events caused by movements in the Earth's crust and are not directly caused by the heating of the atmosphere.

**Step 2:** This means $$ 1 \text{ cm} $$ on the map represents $$ 50,000 \text{ cm} $$ on the actual ground.
**Step 3:** Convert centimeters to kilometers. Since $$ 100,000 \text{ cm} =

questions.stem: One of the following is a sub branch of **physical geography**.
explanation_steps: **Physical Geography** focuses on the natural environment. **Biogeography** is the study of the distribution of species and ecosystems in geographic space and through geological time, making it a core branch of physical geography. Options A and B are approaches to geography, whil

questions.stem: Which one of the following statements is **wrong**?

options.A: deposition is the main work of a river at lower course.
options.B: at the middle course the speed of the river is slower than the upper course.
options.C: load is the eroded materials carried out by a river.
options.D: the upper course of a river is the steepest of all courses.
options.E: erosion and transportation are the main work of a river at the lower course.

explanation_steps: Statement E is wrong because at the **lower course**, the river's energy is low, and its primary work is **deposition**, not erosion and transportation. Erosion and transportation are the dominant processes in the upper and middle courses.

questions.stem: The reasons since 1750 in the size of world population have been a rapid increase.

options.A: the beginning of industrial revolution in Western Europe
options.C: the development of technology in modern transportation

explanation_steps: The rapid growth of the world population since the mid-18th century (the demographic transition) was caused by a combination of the Industrial Revolution (economic growth), medical advancements (lower death rates), and better food production and distribution.

questions.stem: Which of the following are **areas** of world distribution of volcanoes and earthquake?
explanation_steps: Volcanoes and earthquakes are primarily concentrated along tectonic plate boundaries. The **Pacific Ring of Fire**, **Mid-Atlantic Ridge**, and the **Alpine-Himalayan/Mediterranean belts** are the most active seismic and volcanic zones on Earth.

questions.stem: The natural Vegetation types that adapt to **arid and semi arid** condition is described as:
explanation_steps: **Xerophytes** are plants that have evolved special adaptations to survive in environments with very little liquid water, such as deserts (arid and semi-arid regions).

questions.stem: During the Italian colonial rule the largest part of Eritrean **export value** was:
explanation_steps: During the Italian colonial period, while the Italians promoted commercial agriculture (cash crops), **animal products** (specifically hides, skins, and meat) consistently accounted for a very large portion of Eritrea's export value to international markets.

questions.stem: The eastern lowlands of Eritrea are **least important** for:
explanation_steps: The eastern lowlands of Eritrea are characterized by extreme aridity, high temperatures, and poor soil quality. While they are rich in minerals (salt) and have high potential for fishing and geothermal energy, they are **least suitable for agriculture** due to water scarcity.

questions.stem: The contour interval of the map is ___ meters.
explanation_steps:
**Step 1:** Locate two consecutive index contours (bold lines) with values. On this map, we see $$ 1500 $$ and $$ 1000 $$.
**Step 2:** Count the number of spaces (intervals) between these two lines. There are 5 intervals.
**Step 3:** Calculate the difference: $$ 1500 - 1000 = 500

questions.stem: The mountain chains found in the **western coast of North America** known as:
explanation_steps:
The **Rockies** (Rocky Mountains) are the major mountain range located along the western part of North America. 
- **Andes:** South America
- **Alps:** Europe
- **Atlas:** Africa
- **Himalayas:** Asia

questions.stem: The most effective, accurate and commonest ways of representing of heights are:
explanation_steps: **Contour lines** are the most effective and common way to represent relief on a map because they show both the height and the shape of the land (slopes, valleys, hills) continuously.

questions.stem: The natural vegetation of **tropical wet climate** is called:
explanation_steps:
**Selvas** is the term used for the dense, multi-layered tropical rainforests found in the Amazon basin and other tropical wet regions. 
- **Maquis:** Mediterranean
- **Taiga:** Sub-arctic
- **Savannah:** Tropical wet-and-dry

questions.stem: Globally **endangered** animal species found around Gelaelo and Thio:
explanation_steps: The **African Wild Ass** (*Equus africanus*) is a critically endangered species. One of its last remaining natural habitats in the world is the Danakil desert of Eritrea, specifically in the areas around Gelaelo and Thio.

questions.stem: Identify **non characteristics** of crystalline soils:

options.A: they develop in areas with a high degree of weathering
options.C: they are very shallow and in many places the parent rocks are left without soil
options.D: their nitrogen and organic content vary from low to medium

explanation_steps: Crystalline soils (derived from Precambrian basement rocks) are typically **stony and shallow** with a **low degree of weathering** because they often occur on steep slopes where erosion is active. Therefore, saying they have a 'high degree of weathering' is incorrect.

questions.stem: Lines that connect all places with the same **rainfall** is called:
explanation_steps: **Isohyets** are isolines on a map that connect points receiving the same amount of precipitation (rainfall) over a given period.

questions.stem: One of the following is **not proposed protected areas** committed by the government of Eritrea to conserve what remains wild life that we have:
explanation_steps: The government of Eritrea has proposed several protected areas like Gash-Setit (for elephants), Buri-Denakalia (for wild ass), and Semenawi-Bahri (for evergreen forests). The **Hazemo plain** is a major agricultural and grazing zone and is not designated as a primary wildlife pro

questions.stem: Calculate the straight line ground distance between the points **D** and **F**, if the given map distance is $$ 5 \text{ centimeters} $$?
explanation_steps:
**Step 1:** Note the map scale is $$ 1:50,000 $$, which means $$ 1 \text{ cm} = 0.5 \text{ km} $$.
**Step 2:** The map distance given is $$ 5 \text{ cm} $$.
**Step 3:** Multiply map distance by the scale factor: $$ 5 \text{ cm} \times 0.5 \text{ km/cm} = 2.5 \text{ km} $$.

questions.stem: Equatorial region characterized by high temperature, high relative humidity and high rainfall throughout the year. But certain places in it experience low temperature due to:
explanation_steps: Temperature decreases with an increase in **altitude** (height above sea level) at a rate of approximately $$ 6.4^\circ C $$ per $$ 1000 $$ meters. Therefore, high-altitude locations in the equatorial region (like Mt. Kilimanjaro or the Andes) experience much cooler temperatures

questions.stem: The **first three largest islands** of Eritrea are:
explanation_steps: The three largest islands in the Dahlak Archipelago and Eritrea are **Dahlak Kebir** (the largest), **Norah** (second largest), and **Halba** (third largest according to standard curriculum texts).

questions.stem: Which of the following events happened in Eritrea and Horn Africa is **wrongly matched**?

options.A: the land began to sink – Triassic period
options.B: formation of East African Rift Valley – Pliocene epoch
options.C: complete retreat of Indian Ocean – cretaceous period
options.D: the land began to rise– Jurassic period

explanation_steps: During the **Jurassic period**, the land in the Horn of Africa actually **sank** (marine transgression), allowing the Indian Ocean to cover the region. The land began to **rise** (marine regression) later during the Cretaceous period.

questions.stem: The most important factors which have great influence upon **air pressure**:
explanation_steps: Air pressure is primarily influenced by **altitude** (pressure decreases as altitude increases) and **temperature** (warm air is less dense and exerts less pressure than cold air).

questions.stem: ________________________ Mountains are formed by the **solidification of molten** and semi-molten materials
explanation_steps: **Volcanic mountains** are formed when molten rock (magma) from deep within the Earth erupts through the crust and piles up on the surface, solidifying into a mountain shape.

questions.stem: The **uneven population distribution** in Eritrea is determined by:
explanation_steps: Population distribution in Eritrea is highly uneven. It is influenced by physical factors like **altitude** (higher density in the cooler highlands) and **topography**, as well as human factors like **transportation networks** and access to **natural resources** (water and fertil

questions.stem: Which of the following is **correct** statement?

options.A: the sun is the center of the universe.
options.B: the earth rotates from east to west.
options.C: coriolis is the effect of revolution of the earth.
options.E: centripetal force is the sun’s gravitational force.

explanation_steps:
In orbital mechanics, the **Sun's gravitational pull** acts as the **centripetal force** that keeps the planets in their elliptical orbits. 
- A is wrong (Sun is center of Solar System).
- B is wrong (Earth rotates West to East).
- C is wrong (Coriolis is an effect of Rotation).

questions.stem: How many valleys would be crossed if a tourist travels along the **footpath**?
explanation_steps:
**Step 1:** Identify the footpath on the map (the dashed line).
**Step 2:** Look for where the footpath crosses V-shaped contour lines where the 'V' points towards higher elevation. These are valleys.
**Step 3:** Counting along the path from the top left towards the bottom right,

questions.stem: Settlements that developed on a site where houses **spread out in several directions** along major roads will be:
explanation_steps:
A **star-shaped** settlement pattern develops when buildings are constructed along several roads that radiate out from a central point or intersection. 
- **Linear:** Along a single road/river.
- **Grid:** Planned with streets at right angles.
- **Radial:** Similar to star but of

questions.stem: Agricultural system in Eritrea is characterized by the following alternatives **except**:

options.C: wide seasonal fluctuations of product prices
options.E: farmers exposed to unpredictable climatic conditions

explanation_steps: Agriculture in Eritrea is generally characterized by **low** crop yields due to reliance on rain-fed systems, traditional methods, and unpredictable climate. Therefore, 'high crop yield per year' is the exception.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of a **small scale map**?
explanation_steps: A **small scale map** shows a large area with little detail. In map scales, a larger denominator means a smaller scale. 1:25,000,000 is the smallest scale here because 1 unit on the map represents 25 million units on the ground.

questions.stem: The transportation of eroded materials **floats** in the river water like mud, silt and sand:
explanation_steps: **Suspended load** consists of very fine particles (clay, silt, and fine sand) that are held up by the turbulence of the water and 'float' within the stream as it flows.

questions.stem: One of the following is **not** a problem of cities in developed countries:
explanation_steps: All the listed options—**traffic congestion, ghettoes, noise pollution, and urban decay**—are common problems faced by major cities in developed nations. Therefore, 'None of the above' is the correct answer to the question 'which is NOT a problem'.

questions.stem: Which of the following is **not** members of the **outer planets**?
explanation_steps: The **outer planets** (Jovian planets) are Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune. **Mars** is one of the four **inner planets** (terrestrial planets), along with Mercury, Venus, and Earth.

questions.stem: All of the following are features produced by wave erosion **except**:
explanation_steps: A **spit** is a landform created by **marine deposition** (sand and gravel moved by longshore drift). Stacks, arches, cliffs, and caves are all landforms created by the **erosive** power of waves hitting the coast.

questions.stem: The average gradient / slope along the straight line **AB (4cm)** is:
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Find Vertical Interval (VI).** Point A is at $$ 1300 \text{ m} $$ and Point B is at $$ 1000 \text{ m} $$. $$ VI = 1300 - 1000 = 300 \text{ m} $$.
**Step 2: Find Horizontal Equivalent (HE).** Map distance is $$ 4 \text{ cm} $$. Using the scale ($$ 1 \text{ cm} = 500 \tex

questions.stem: Basically **all soils** are derived from:
explanation_steps: Soil formation (pedogenesis) begins with the weathering of **parent material**, which can be bedrock or transported deposits. This material determines the initial chemical and mineralogical composition of the soil.

questions.stem: A resource management method based on **reuse** is:
explanation_steps: **Recycling** is the process of converting waste materials into new materials and objects. It is a form of resource management that emphasizes the reuse of materials to reduce the consumption of fresh raw materials.

questions.stem: One of the following is a **correct** statement:

options.A: population Geography is a sub branch of Physical Geography
options.B: life expectancy is the average number of years a person expects to live
options.C: population density is the spread of people on the earth’s surface
options.D: expansive pyramid indicates slow population growth of all age groups

explanation_steps:
**Life expectancy** is defined as the statistical measure of the average time an organism is expected to live. 
- A is wrong (it's Human Geography).
- C is wrong (that's population distribution; density is people per area).
- D is wrong (expansive means rapid growth).

questions.stem: Which zone is characterized by **hot and wet** seasons?
explanation_steps: The **Equatorial** climate zone is characterized by consistently high temperatures and high rainfall throughout the year, making it perennially 'hot and wet'.

questions.stem: In which layer of the atmosphere **constant change of weather** and climate occurs?
explanation_steps: The **Troposphere** is the lowest layer of the atmosphere where almost all weather phenomena (clouds, rain, wind) occur because it contains most of the atmosphere's water vapor and mass.

questions.stem: The landforms of ocean crust are part of continental crust **except** they covered by water are:

options.A: ocean deep and deep sea plain
options.D: deep sea plain and ocean ridge

explanation_steps: The **continental shelf** and **continental slope** are geologically part of the continental crust, even though they are submerged under the ocean. The true 'oceanic crust' begins beyond the continental rise at the deep-sea plain.

questions.stem: Which of the following is **cultural geographic feature**?
explanation_steps: Cultural geographic features are man-made elements of the landscape. An **industrial region** is created by human economic activity. Savannah, escarpments, soil, and coastal areas are all physical (natural) features.

questions.stem: Which of the following points is **located** on a valley bottom?
explanation_steps: Point **R** is located where the contour lines form a sharp 'V' shape pointing towards the higher ground (uphill). This pattern is characteristic of a valley or a river course. Points like K and H are on slopes or spurs.

questions.stem: All planets move along their own **fixed path**. This is due to:

options.B: the revolution and axial tilt toward the sun
options.D: the elliptical shape and axial tilted

explanation_steps: Planets stay in orbit due to the balance between the Sun's gravitational pull (**centripetal force**) pulling them inward and their own inertia (**centrifugal force**) pushing them outward. This balance keeps them on a fixed elliptical path.

questions.stem: Before construct of a dam we must carefully study all of the following **except**:
explanation_steps: All the factors listed (geology, catchment area, safety, and accessibility) are critical considerations in the planning and construction of a dam. Therefore, 'None of the above' is the correct choice as an exception.

questions.stem: Identify the **false** statement from the following:

options.B: solar radiation reaches the ground as short waves
options.C: radiated energy back to the atmosphere as long waves
options.D: the earth radiates heat to the atmosphere both day and night

explanation_steps: All statements A, B, C, and D are scientifically correct. Insolation is daytime only, solar input is shortwave, terrestrial output is longwave, and the Earth emits radiation continuously (day and night). Therefore, 'None of the above' is the correct choice.

questions.stem: Rural settlements are **distinguished** from urban settlements by:
explanation_steps: The primary geographical distinction between rural and urban areas is the **economic activity**. Rural areas are dominated by **primary activities** (agriculture, fishing, mining), while urban areas focus on **secondary and tertiary activities** (industry, services).

questions.stem: The **Summer and winter rainfalls** in Eritrea are:
explanation_steps: In Eritrea, summer rainfall (in the highlands) is primarily **convectional** (due to intense heating) and **orographic** (moist air rising over mountains). Winter rainfall (on the eastern coast) is also largely **orographic** as moist winds from the Red Sea hit the escarpment.

questions.stem: One of the following is **true** characteristic of the **sub tropical desert climate**:

options.A: the daily range of temperature is very high.

explanation_steps: Subtropical deserts are known for having a **very high daily (diurnal) range of temperature**. Because of the clear skies and low humidity, days are extremely hot, and nights are very cold as heat escapes rapidly.

questions.stem: Which of the following is **not** the measure of water conservation?

options.A: prevents or minimizes Siltation of surface water reservoirs
options.B: minimizes consumption and protect from contamination
options.C: makes wise use of the existing water supply

explanation_steps: Water conservation focuses on sustainable management and saving water. While 'maximizing utility' sounds positive, in resource management, it often refers to intensive extraction and use, which can lead to depletion. Standard conservation measures include preventing siltation, re

questions.stem: Point **T** is located on a:
explanation_steps: Point **T** is situated between two higher peaks (marked as 8 and another high point). A low point or a dip between two higher areas of ground is called a **saddle** or a **col**.

questions.stem: The German meteorologist who proposed the theory of **continental drift** in 1912 was:
explanation_steps: **Alfred Wegener** proposed the Continental Drift theory in 1912, suggesting that all continents were once joined in a single supercontinent called **Pangaea** before drifting apart.

questions.stem: One of the following statements is **false** about the relief of Eritrea?

options.B: it contains different types of physical features
options.C: elevation varies from 116 meter above Sea level. to 3000 meter below sea level.

explanation_steps: Statement C is false. The elevation of Eritrea varies from approximately **116 meters below sea level** (in the Danakil Depression) to **3018 meters above sea level** (Mount Soira). The statement incorrectly swaps 'above' and 'below' and uses incorrect numbers.

questions.stem: There was a single **super ocean** about 250 million years ago called:
explanation_steps: While **Pangaea** was the single supercontinent, **Panthalassa** was the vast global ocean that surrounded it during the late Paleozoic and early Mesozoic eras.

questions.stem: The **most populated** country in Africa is:
explanation_steps: **Nigeria** is the most populous country in Africa, with a population exceeding 200 million people. It is followed by Ethiopia and Egypt.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a **correct** statement about a region?

options.A: Two places on the earth’s surface are exactly the same.
options.B: every place on the earth is a unique.
options.C: unifying elements are grouped together to create regions.
options.D: the unifying factor diminishes as we move towards the center.

explanation_steps: In geography, every place is **unique** (B). A **region** is an area defined by one or more **unifying characteristics** (C) that distinguish it from surrounding areas. Therefore, both B and C are correct.

questions.stem: **Rift valley** and **block mountains** are the result of:
explanation_steps: **Faulting** (the cracking and displacement of rock layers due to tension or compression) creates features like **Rift Valleys** (grabens) and **Block Mountains** (horsts). The East African Rift Valley is a classic example.

questions.stem: Polar climates are known for:
explanation_steps: Polar climates (found in the Arctic and Antarctic) are defined by having average temperatures below $$ 10^\circ C $$ even in the warmest months, resulting in **permanently cold conditions**.

questions.stem: If the length and the width of the given map are $$ 18 $$ and $$ 14 \text{ centimeters} $$ respectively. **Half** of the total surface area covered by the map is __________ square kilometers.
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Convert map dimensions to ground dimensions.** Scale is $$ 1 \text{ cm} = 0.5 \text{ km} $$.
- Ground Length = $$ 18 \text{ cm} \times 0.5 = 9 \text{ km} $$.
- Ground Width = $$ 14 \text{ cm} \times 0.5 = 7 \text{ km} $$.
**Step 2: Calculate total area.** $$ \text{Area}

questions.stem: The **most** widely used economic measure of development is:
explanation_steps: While the **Human Development Index (HDI)** is a more comprehensive measure (including health and education), **per capita income** (GNI or GDP per person) remains the most widely used *purely economic* indicator to compare the wealth of nations.

questions.stem: Identify the **correct** statement about trade winds:

options.C: blow only towards sub polar low

explanation_steps: **Trade winds** are permanent east-to-west prevailing winds that flow in the Earth's equatorial region. They originate from the **sub-tropical high-pressure belts** (around 30° N/S) and blow towards the Equatorial Low-pressure belt (ITCZ).

questions.stem: Fossil soils or rocks are made up of:
explanation_steps: In the geological context of Eritrea, 'fossil soils' (paleosols) often refer to the lateritic layers formed by intense weathering before the volcanic eruptions of the Cenozoic. These are rich in **iron oxide** (giving a red color) and **kaolin** (clay).

questions.stem: Which of the following relief features on a map points towards the **lower ground**?
explanation_steps: On a contour map, **V-shaped** contour lines that point towards **lower ground** represent a **Spur** (a piece of high ground jutting into a valley). Conversely, V-shaped contours pointing towards higher ground represent a Valley.

questions.stem: Which of the following is **not** a metamorphosed Precambrian rock?
explanation_steps: **Diorite** is an intrusive **igneous rock**, not a metamorphic rock. Gneiss, Schist, Phyllite, and Marble are all examples of metamorphic rocks (formed by heat and pressure).

questions.stem: A horizon in a soil profile consists of **partially weathered bed rock** is:
explanation_steps: The **C Horizon** (parent material) consists of large lumps of partially broken down (weathered) bedrock. It sits above the unweathered bedrock (R Horizon) and below the subsoil (B Horizon).

questions.stem: Soil **texture** helps to determine:

options.C: vertical cross section of a soil
options.D: porosity and permeability of a soil

explanation_steps: Soil texture refers to the size of the mineral particles (sand, silt, clay). This physical property directly determines the **porosity** (amount of air space) and **permeability** (how easily water flows through), which are vital for plant growth.

questions.stem: Where is the bearing of point **B** from point **S** on the map?
explanation_steps: To find the bearing of B from S, place a compass rose at point S. Point B is located in the direction between North and East. Therefore, the direction is **Northeast**.

questions.stem: Widely spaced evergreen vegetation along eastern escarpment outside **Green belt** is:
explanation_steps: The 'Green Belt' of Eritrea (Filfil Solomuna) is a tropical coniferous forest. The area surrounding/outside it on the eastern escarpment typically transitions into **semi-humid woodland** before reaching the more arid coastal plains.

questions.stem: Which of the following is **not** moderate densely populated area?
explanation_steps: **Humid tropics** (like the Amazon or Congo basins) are generally **sparsely populated** due to dense rainforests, poor soils (leaching), and high prevalence of tropical diseases. They do not fit the 'moderate' density category like grasslands or coastal areas.

questions.stem: The layers that fold **bend up** and **down bend** respectively:
explanation_steps: In structural geology, an **anticline** is a fold that is convex up (bends up), and a **syncline** is a fold that is concave up (bends down).

questions.stem: Due to its tropical location Eritrea has a huge **potential** for:
explanation_steps: Because Eritrea is located in the tropics (close to the equator) and has many cloudless days, especially in the lowlands, it receives intense sunlight throughout the year, giving it a high potential for **solar energy**.

questions.stem: One of the following is **not** the problem of water resources in the western lowlands and western escarpments of Eritrea?

options.B: low recharge rate of ground water
options.C: saline ground water and high rate of Siltation
options.E: depletion of ground water due to heavy pumping for irrigation

explanation_steps: While meager rainfall, low recharge, high evaporation, and depletion are significant issues in the western lowlands, **saline ground water** is generally more of a specific problem in the **coastal/eastern lowlands** due to seawater intrusion, rather than a primary regional probl

questions.stem: The time when the sun in the Northern hemisphere on **June 21** is known as:
explanation_steps: On **June 21**, the Sun is directly overhead at the Tropic of Cancer ($$ 23.5^\circ N $$). This is the **Summer Solstice** for the Northern Hemisphere, marking the longest day of the year.

questions.stem: One of the following is **not** the effect of **rotation** of the earth:
explanation_steps: **Cold winters** (seasons) are caused by the Earth's **revolution** around the Sun and the tilt of its axis. Rotation causes daily phenomena like day/night cycles (mornings/dusks), the Coriolis effect, and local winds like sea breezes.

questions.stem: Which of the following pairs of points is **not** inter-visible?
explanation_steps: Inter-visibility means two points can 'see' each other without any obstruction. Between point **9** (high ground) and point **B** (lower ground), there is a ridge or a higher contour line that blocks the line of sight. Therefore, they are not inter-visible.

questions.stem: State the difference between **concave slope** and **convex slope**? (2pts)
questions.answer: Concave slope: Steep at the top and gentle at the bottom. Convex slope: Gentle at the top and steep at the bottom.
accepted_answers: Concave slope: Steep at the top and gentle at the bottom. Convex slope: Gentle at the top and steep at the bottom.
explanation_steps: A **concave slope** has contour lines that are closely spaced at higher elevations (steep) and widely spaced at lower elevations (gentle). A **convex slope** is the opposite; contour lines are widely spaced at the top (gentle) and closely spaced at the bottom (steep).

questions.stem: What are the two advantages of **surface water development**? (2 pts)
questions.answer: 1. Irrigation for agriculture. 2. Hydroelectric power (HEP) generation.
accepted_answers: 1. Irrigation for agriculture. 2. Hydroelectric power (HEP) generation.
explanation_steps:
Surface water development (like dams and reservoirs) provides: 
1. **Irrigation**: Reliable water for crops in dry regions.
2. **Hydroelectric Power**: Renewable energy generation.
3. **Domestic Supply**: Clean water for drinking and industrial use.

questions.stem: Why **wind erosion** is more powerful in hot desert areas? (1pt)
questions.answer: Due to the lack of vegetation cover and the presence of loose, dry surface materials.
accepted_answers: Due to the lack of vegetation cover and the presence of loose, dry surface materials.
explanation_steps:
Wind erosion is dominant in deserts because:
1. **Lack of vegetation**: There are no plants to anchor the soil or act as windbreaks.
2. **Aridity**: The soil is dry and loose, making it easy for the wind to lift and transport particles.

questions.stem: Write down three most important **fishing grounds** of the world? (3pts)
questions.answer: 1. Northwest Pacific. 2. Northeast Atlantic. 3. Northwest Atlantic.
accepted_answers: 1. Northwest Pacific. 2. Northeast Atlantic. 3. Northwest Atlantic.
explanation_steps:
The world's major fishing grounds are:
1. **Northwest Pacific**: Around Japan and Russia.
2. **Northeast Atlantic**: Western Europe and North Sea.
3. **Northwest Atlantic**: The Grand Banks of Newfoundland.
4. **Southeast Pacific**: Off the coast of Peru.

questions.stem: Why do we say the **strategic position of Eritrea** depends on the Red Sea’s geographic location? (2pts)
questions.answer: Because it controls a long coastline along one of the world's busiest maritime trade routes connecting Europe, Asia, and Africa.
accepted_answers: Because it controls a long coastline along one of the world's busiest maritime trade routes connecting Europe, Asia, and Africa.

questions.stem:
Define the following words as a **geographical term**? (1pt)
1. **Region**
2. **Scale**
questions.answer: 1. Region: An area with unifying characteristics. 2. Scale: The ratio between map distance and ground distance.
accepted_answers: 1. Region: An area with unifying characteristics. 2. Scale: The ratio between map distance and ground distance.
explanation_steps:
1. **Region**: A basic unit of geographical study defined by unifying physical or human characteristics.
2. **Scale**: The mathematical relationship between the distance on a map and the actual distance on the Earth's surface.

questions.stem: The **gradient /slope** between any two points on a contour map can be expressed into three ways. Mention two of them? (2pts)
questions.answer: 1. As a Ratio. 2. As a Percentage. 3. As an Angle.
accepted_answers: 1. As a Ratio. 2. As a Percentage. 3. As an Angle.
explanation_steps:
Gradient measures the steepness of a slope and can be expressed as:
1. **Ratio**: e.g., 1 in 50.
2. **Percentage**: e.g., 2% (Vertical Interval / Horizontal Equivalent * 100).
3. **Angle**: Expressed in degrees.

questions.stem: Give two examples of **inorganic components** of a soil? (2pts)
questions.answer: 1. Mineral particles (sand, silt, clay). 2. Soil water and soil air.
accepted_answers: 1. Mineral particles (sand, silt, clay). 2. Soil water and soil air.
explanation_steps: Soil is composed of organic and inorganic matter. **Inorganic components** include minerals derived from the parent rock (sand, silt, clay), as well as water and air trapped in soil pores.

questions.stem: List the four common **characteristics of all regions**? (2pts)
explanation_steps:
All geographical regions share four basic traits:
1. **Location**: A specific position on Earth.
2. **Area**: Occupation of a certain amount of space.
3. **Boundaries**: Limits that separate it from other areas.
4. **Unifying Characteristics**: Common physical or cultural feature
